item.title: CNCF Research Shows Virtual Machines Remain Central as AI Workloads Evolve
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/cncf-vm-ai-workloads/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794993904528.jpg"/><p>New research from the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) and Linux Foundation Research finds that VMs host an average of 53% of production applications, while emerging AI and agentic workloads are creating additional demand for virtualisation, particularly where stronger execution isolation is required.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

item.title: CNCF Research Shows Virtual Machines Remain Central as AI Workloads Evolve
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/cncf-vm-ai-workloads/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794993904528.jpg"/><p>New research from the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) and Linux Foundation Research finds that VMs host an average of 53% of production applications, while emerging AI and agentic workloads are creating additional demand for virtualisation, particularly where stronger execution isolation is required.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

item.title: OpenAI Scales Git for Coding Agents with Pando
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/openai-git-pando/en/headerimage/openai-pando-header-1795331180238.jpeg"/><p>OpenAI has detailed Pando, a new backend that scales Git for concurrent coding-agent workloads without replacing familiar Git workflows. The company reports nearly 80% lower median push latency by coordinating branch updates independently and reusing stored packfiles across fetches.</p> <i>By Eran Stiller</i>

item.title: Presentation: Inferencing for Enterprises
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/enterprise-ai-inference-architecture-costs/en/mediumimage/dio-rettori-medium-1793800900455.jpeg"/><p>Dio Rettori discusses the operational realities of enterprise AI inference. Moving beyond fast token generation, he explores why inference requires dedicated systems engineering, tackles GPU utilization pitfalls, compares on-prem versus cloud TCO, and analyzes multi-agent latency determinism. He shares why teams must embed domain ontology directly into models rather than relying solely on RAG.</p> <i>By Dio Rettori</i>

item.title: Article: Engineering Around Non-Determinism: Evals, Grounding, and Release Gates for AI-Drafted Suspicious Reports
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/llm-agent-architecture-evals-grounding/en/headerimage/llm-agent-architecture-evals-grounding-header-1795173682566.jpg"/><p>Moving GenAI into high-stakes production requires treating non-determinism as an engineering problem. This architectural blueprint shows engineering leaders and architects how to build trustworthy agentic workflows using knowledge graphs, dual-layer eval judges, CI/CD release gates, and regression testing against golden datasets to automate drafting while maintaining zero-hallucination compliance.</p> <i>By Ritesh Modi, Sasidhar Gudala</i>

item.title: QCon San Francisco 2026: Lessons from Building a $100M Product in Six Weeks at OpenAI
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/qcon-sf-openai-lessons/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1795453078651.jpg"/><p>At QCon San Francisco 2026, OpenAI's Brian Yang described building the ChatGPT ads product with Codex agents and no human-written code. He outlined layered testing, sandboxes, and batched pull request reviews, and noted failure modes such as code "slop" and unsafe agent actions. He advised gradual adoption and framed engineers as managers of agents.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: QCon San Francisco 2026: Securing AI Agents in Production
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/qcon-ai-agent-security/en/headerimage/header-1795213847070.jpeg"/><p>At QCon San Francisco, Google's Amanda Walker framed AI agents as an insider-risk problem operating at machine speed, and described identity, credential and containment patterns for running them safely in production.</p> <i>By Mark Silvester</i>

item.title: QCon San Francisco 2026: Securing AI Agents in Production

item.title: How LinkedIn Built a View-Agnostic Analytics System for Modern iOS UI Architectures
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/linkedin-view-agnostic-analytics/en/headerimage/linkedin-view-agnostic-analytics-1795455502517.jpeg"/><p>To address the challenge posed by modern iOS UI systems where the logical UI structure may not mirror the native UIKit hierarchy, LinkedIn engineers developed a view-agnostic analytics system build around a shared MeasurableNode contract.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

item.title: JEP 545 Moves ZGC Memory Preparation off the Startup Path in JDK 28
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/jep-545-jdk-28/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1795265408975.jpg"/><p>JEP 545, Faster Startup and Warmup with ZGC, has been integrated into JDK 28, moving heap memory preparation onto concurrent worker threads. ZGC now pre-touches memory as it expands and upgrades small pages to large ones on Linux 6.1 and later, but the 2 MB initial heap behind the JEP's 38% startup and 90% warmup gains requires the adaptive heap sizing flag from JEP 546, which is off by default.</p> <i>By A N M Bazlur Rahman</i>

item.title: JEP 545 Moves ZGC Memory Preparation off the Startup Path in JDK 28
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/jep-545-jdk-28/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1795265408975.jpg"/><p>JEP 545, Faster Startup and Warmup with ZGC, has been integrated into JDK 28, moving heap memory preparation onto concurrent worker threads. ZGC now pre-touches memory as it expands and upgrades small pages to large ones on Linux 6.1 and later, but the 2 MB initial heap behind the JEP's 38% startup and 90% warmup gains requires the adaptive heap sizing flag from JEP 546, which is off by default.</p> <i>By A N M Bazlur Rahman</i>

item.title: Java News Roundup: Java4Shell, Oracle CSPUs, OpenJDK, Azul Payara, BellSoft, Helidon, LangChain4j
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/java-news-roundup-nov16-2026/en/headerimage/java-news-roundup-image-1795447387323.jpg"/><p>This week's Java roundup for November 16th, 2026, features news highlighting: the Java4Shell RCE vulnerability; Oracle CSPUs; Lazy Constants targeted for JDK 28; the November 2026 edition of Azul Payara; point releases of Java Operator SDK, LangChain4j and Micrometer; maintenance releases of Liberica JDK and Helidon; and second release candidates of Hibernate Reactive.</p> <i>By Michael Redlich</i>

item.title: Netflix at QConSF 2026: Retrofitting the SDLC for AI Coding Agents
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/netflix-sdlc-ai-coding-agents/en/headerimage/netflix-header-1200x630-1795359626158.jpg"/><p>At QCon San Francisco 2026, Mark Khuzam of Netflix explained how the Commerce team retrofitted its SDLC so AI coding agents and engineers could ship together. The team wrote 45 architecture decision records for people and agents, added a review agent that posts only verified blockers, and serves per-domain GraphRAG context through a single MCP tool.</p> <i>By Andrew Hoblitzell</i>

item.title: Agoda Reduces API Code Review Time by 64% with Modular Architecture
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/agoda-modular-monolith-framework/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793569078425.jpg"/><p>Agoda introduced a modular monolith framework in its post-booking API to reduce coupling without a full rewrite. The platform uses domain components, Data Mapper patterns, typed builders, and ArchUnit tests to enforce boundaries. Framework-backed changes showed 64% shorter median code reviews and 34% faster initial feedback than legacy changes.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

item.title: Claude Code Adds Experimental Code Mode to Orchestrate Tool Calls with JavaScript
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/claude-code-mode/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1795090945761.jpg"/><p>Anthropic's experimental Code Mode lets Claude Code write JavaScript that chains, parallelizes, and filters Bash, Read, and Edit calls, with changes to how auto mode and hooks review those calls.</p> <i>By Daniel Dominguez</i>

item.title: Claude Code Adds Experimental Code Mode to Orchestrate Tool Calls with JavaScript

item.title: Podcast: Simulation Can Tell You What Your Agents are Actually Doing: A Conversation with Zhou Yu
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/podcasts/simulation-agents-actually-doing/en/smallimage/infoq-podcast-500-1794910149760.jpg"/><p>Michael Stiefel spoke to Zhou Yu about using dynamic simulations to evaluate AI agents. One particular focus was conversational agents where actions depend on prior responses, and the non-deterministic nation of LLMs means you cannot rely on static, reference-based benchmarks. You need to test them using dynamic simulations that incorporate different personas, goals, and corner cases.</p> <i>By Zhou Yu</i>

item.title: QCon San Francisco 2026: The Harness Is the New Operating System
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/harness-new-operating-system/en/headerimage/harness-header-1200x630-1795301479582.jpg"/><p>At QCon San Francisco 2026, Mad Labs founder and CEO Manju Rajashekhar opened the conference arguing that the harness around an AI model, rather than the model itself, decides what an agent can do and how safely it does it. The keynote mapped the parts of a harness, including context, tools, state, permissions and feedback loops, onto jobs that operating systems already perform.</p> <i>By Andrew Hoblitzell</i>

item.title: PostgreSQL 19 Released with Online Table Repacking and Query Planning Controls
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/postgresql-19-released/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1795349035334.jpg"/><p>The PostgreSQL Global Development Group released PostgreSQL 19, introducing changes to database maintenance, query planning, replication, and application development. The release focuses on reducing administrative overhead and improving performance, with new tools for reorganizing tables without downtime and controlling query plans.</p> <i>By Robert Krzaczyński</i>

item.title: Claude Code Has Been Leaking Secrets through its "Don't Ask Again" Feature
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/claude-code-leaking-secrets/en/headerimage/linux-6-12-real-time-1795344939763.jpeg"/><p>Agentic security firm Apiiro found that Claude Code has been exposing secrets in public repositories due to how it stores them in local file on developers' machines to implement "Don't Ask Again". The company identified 1,122 secrets in claude/settings.local.json files and another 1,160 in git history, in the shared settings.json, and in agent chat transcripts stored in repos.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

item.title: AWS Lambda Now Runs GPU Inference with 48 Concurrent Invocations Sharing One Model per GPU
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/aws-lambda-gpu-managed-instances/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1795178998128.jpg"/><p>AWS Lambda now runs Event Functions on EC2 G-series GPU instances through Lambda Managed Instances, with up to 48 concurrent invocations sharing one model per GPU, vLLM and SGLang base images that need no handler code, and 90-minute asynchronous timeouts. Billing is the instance price plus a 9.75 percent fee; first hands-on tests report an eight-minute publish and no response streaming.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: Grafana 13.3 Adds Shared Dashboard Variables and Notebooks
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/grafana-13-3-shared-variables/en/headerimage/header-1795209346746.jpeg"/><p>Grafana 13.3 introduces shared variables across dashboards and adds Notebooks to record investigations. Both features are in public preview and require feature toggles for self-managed installations.</p> <i>By Mark Silvester</i>

item.title: How Google Traced GKE API Timeouts to a Linux Kernel TCP Bug
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/gke-kernel-network-bug/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794082671635.jpg"/><p>Google recently detailed how three interacting bugs across Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), Private Service Connect, and the Linux kernel caused intermittent Kubernetes API connectivity failures, blocking around 800 developers from deploying to production.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

item.title: Google Donates Agent Substrate and gVisor to the CNCF to Secure AI Agents at Scale
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/google-substrate-gvisor-cncf/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794408775099.jpg"/><p>Google has announced it is donating Agent Substrate and gVisor to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF), placing two important components of its AI agent infrastructure under vendor-neutral open-source governance.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

item.title: Presentation: Modernising Retail at Scale: Architecting a Cloud‑to‑Edge Platform for a Global Enterprise
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/tesco-enterprise-tech-transformation/en/mediumimage/JayeshBhayani-medium-1792654742095.jpg"/><p>Jayesh Bhayani discusses Tesco’s decade-long enterprise transformation from fragmented legacy systems to a unified cloud-edge platform. He explains how aligning system, talent, and process modernizations allowed Tesco to scale mission-critical retail operations to millions of customers, while sharing practical lessons on build vs. buy, cloud cost management, and preparing for agentic commerce.</p> <i>By Jayesh Bhayani</i>

item.title: Article: Building Reliability into the Cloud: Observability as the Control Plane for Multi-Region Failover
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/observability-control-plane-failover/en/headerimage/header-1795002929606.jpg"/><p>Cloud SLAs promise uptime statistically, not absolutely. This article shows how to treat observability as a control plane that detects regional degradation, triggers automated failover, and confirms recovery rather than paging a human. Covers active-active architecture, DNS TTL pitfalls, composite Prometheus alerting, Route 53 weighted routing, and confirmation loops backed by a real S3 outage.</p> <i>By Saurabh Ahuja</i>

item.title: AWS Releases a Free Local Emulator of AWS Built Entirely by Agents
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/aws-emulator-local-testing/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1795086946449.jpg"/><p>AWS has released AWS Emulator, a free, CC0-licensed local stand-in for more than 200 of its services, generated from its public API models and aimed at the test loops of coding agents. AWS says agents wrote and maintain all of the code and publishes per-release fidelity scores. The docs say it does not evaluate IAM, and practitioners are split on trusting an emulator nobody reviewed.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: Presentation: AI-Assisted Software Delivery: from Code to Production
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/ai-assisted-software-delivery/en/mediumimage/infoq-live-medium-1795097572325.jpg"/><p>The panelists explore how engineering teams adapt delivery architectures, pipelines, security, and governance for AI-assisted development. They share practical strategies for verifying AI-generated code, solving testing and deployment bottlenecks, maintaining human oversight, and measuring AI’s true impact on software velocity, quality, reliability, and operational cost.</p> <i>By Garima Bajpaj, Martin Reynolds, Patrick Debois, Gunnar Grosch, Renato Losio</i>

item.title: LinkedIn Cuts Daily Spark Shuffle Fetch Failures from 750 to 20 with Apache Celeborn
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>LinkedIn deployed Apache Celeborn as a shared remote shuffle platform across most Spark and Flink workloads, reducing daily shuffle fetch failures from approximately 750 to 20. The deployment also lowered compute costs by 10%, improved application runtimes by 14%, and reduced shuffle costs per task by nearly 90% through dedicated storage, replication, and data-plane optimizations.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

item.title: AWS PrivateLink Tunnel Endpoints Open a Whole CIDR Range to Another Account
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/aws-privatelink-tunnel-endpoints/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794476042263.jpg"/><p>AWS has detailed tunnel endpoints, a PrivateLink endpoint type that gives a consumer VPC access to an entire network segment in another account rather than one resource at a time, over an overlapping address space and with consumer-initiated connections only. The consumer must wrap traffic in GENEVE; only TCP and DNS pass, and access logs cannot attribute traffic to a workload behind the endpoint.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: Yelp Migrates Cassandra to EKS by Moving EBS Volumes
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/kubernetes-cassandra-eks/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794921404342.jpg"/><p>Yelp has moved its Cassandra fleet from legacy self-managed Kubernetes clusters to Amazon EKS by re-pointing existing EBS volumes at new pods, rather than streaming data between nodes.</p> <i>By Claudio Masolo</i>

item.title: Qwik 2.0 RC: Replaces HTML Comment Markers for Faster Reactivity and Out-of-Order Streaming
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/quik-2-streaming/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794907611481.jpg"/><p>Qwik 2.0 Release Candidate, published on 1 October 2026, replaces v1's HTML comment markers with two script blocks that hold state and virtual node data. It adds experimental out-of-order streaming, async useComputed$, and cacheable route loaders. Qwik's benchmarks show v2 at 1.23x vanilla JavaScript, versus 2.59x for v1. A migration command is provided.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: GitHub Rebuilds the Copilot App's Diff Surface to Open Million-Line Pull Requests without Jank
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/github-pull-requests-rebuild/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794747791339.jpg"/><p>GitHub engineers rebuilt the diff view in the Copilot app to handle a pull request with 2,200 files, over a million changed lines and 400 inline comments. The design separates fixed-height code rows from variable-height comment blocks, which are measured in batches near the viewport. Performance is checked through CI budgets and automated app runs.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: Node.js Brings Debounce, Throttle, and PKCS#12 Parsing into Core Modules
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/nodejs-debounce-throttle/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794593143949.jpg"/><p>Node.js 26.10.0 adds util.debounce() and util.throttle(), plus util.markPromiseAsHandled(), to the core library. It also introduces crypto.parsePKCS12() for reading .p12 and .pfx bundles, and extends the experimental Virtual File System to node:ffi. The additions reduce the need for some userland dependencies. Node.js 26 is now Active LTS.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: Dropbox Shares How its In-House Cookie Auditor Tests Consent Behaviour across 200+ Web Surfaces
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/dropbox-cookie-auditor/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794331089979.jpg"/><p>Dropbox engineers described a Playwright-based auditor that checks cookie consent behavior across more than 200 web surfaces. It runs three tests per page: US visitor, EU visitor, and Global Privacy Control signal. Cookie rules are kept outside the code. A companion tool finds live URLs. Weekly reports separate likely violations from false positives.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>
